decisions: Criterion 5 / umbrella criterion 1 - a published number says whether a rule produced it; the score view's payload is published the moment a caller keeps one, and three coupled scenarios capture 133 of its numbers each.
Criterion 3 - a view's inputs are exactly Program and WalkResult, so the writer choice is a `_leaves` parameter like the other four views' and never a third input on a front door.
Criterion 17 - the S4 allocation ratchet is never relaxed; the optimizer's own evaluations keep DISCARD and say so at their call site.
R-17/D-97 - landed against the committed coupled baseline plus this allowlist; the baseline is re-captured at the phase boundary, never here.

change.one_sentence: The score view's payload carries a dispositions map for every caller that keeps it; the optimizer, which throws thousands of them away per search, opts out through build_participant_timeline(published=False).
change.wire_shape: Every published number keeps its value and its position; the three score-mode scenarios gain the sibling map.

qualifying_population.rule: One new leaf per captured score-mode combat payload; leaf_report treats the whole map as one leaf, so no scenario contributes more than one. The score-mode scenarios are exactly those with score_mode=True in COUPLED_SCENARIOS.

measured.pair_golden: zero diffs - the score payload is coupled-path output and golden enters through pipeline.run_fight (D-93).
measured.transition: absent_to_value on every one - a block that did not exist at capture, not a number that changed

allocation_probe.cassiopeia_3champ: 274347 bytes against the recorded 262196 and a 15% margin (ceiling 301525) - +4.6%, inside the ratchet

measured.allocation_note: Binding a real writer in every score payload was measured first and rejected: cassiopeia_3champ went to 313915 bytes, +19.7% on the recorded peak and past the 15% ceiling. Criterion 17 says that gate is never relaxed, so the optimizer keeps DISCARD and the caller says so.

oracle_pass.why: R-19 asks an investigator to adjudicate between an old value and a new one. All three occurrences are absent_to_value on a schema block that did not exist when the baseline was captured: there is no old value and no arithmetic to reproduce from cached wiki text.
oracle_pass.numeric_evidence: tests/test_payload_dispositions.py::TestTheScoreModePayload asserts two-way key-set equality over all three score-mode scenarios against live runs, and asserts the discarding and recording payloads are equal outside the map itself.

landed_against.rule: R-17/R-32/D-97 - no baseline moves inside this commit
